summary: Backend-only verification of the 3 security fixes (SEC-001 rate limits, SEC-002 attachment MIME + size, SEC-003 partial). New targeted suite /app/backend/tests/test_security_fixes.py (20 tests) + full existing regression suites (/app/backend/tests/test_quota_backend.py = 19 tests, /app/backend/tests/test_close_email_fix.py = 5 tests). Final serial run (-n 0 per pytest.ini sanctioned mode): 44 passed, 0 failed. All 7 features/bugs listed in the review request are verified. The three fixes are CONFIRMED WORKING with no regression on auth, config, blocks CRUD, expenses CRUD, totals, close+email (undeliverable + delivered paths), 24-block pruning, resend-email, export year PDF, and delete block. Mongo email_rate_log and all seeded test docs cleaned up post-run.
action_items: No action needed - all 3 security fixes verified working as specified.

Minor nice-to-have (not blocking): close_block calls _check_rate_limit as first action, which means the rate_log is incremented BEFORE the 'already closed' 400 check. In practice a client cannot double-close a block via the API (status guard), but if an attacker loops close() on an already-closed block they can still exhaust the user's own quota (DoS-self). Low priority; current behavior matches the spec's 'incr-first' assumption.
critical_code_review_comments: _check_rate_limit uses count_documents + insert_one; the two ops are not atomic, so under high concurrency a burst could marginally exceed the quota (<=1 extra). TTL index on email_rate_log.ts (2 days) is correct.

_validate_attachment correctly computes decoded size WITHOUT allocating the decoded blob (uses len(clean)*3//4 heuristic). This avoids large memory alloc. Note: it rounds down, so the exact boundary (decoded == 3MB) passes; values clearly > 3MB are rejected as required.
_validate_attachment is called on POST /expenses and PUT /expenses, both verified. It is NOT called on resend/export (correct - those don't accept attachments).
Rate limit isolation is correct: _check_rate_limit filters by user_id, user2 is not blocked when user1 is at quota (verified end-to-end).
No MongoDB _id leaks in any tested response path.
Minor code smell: 'Blocco chiuso' error on PUT/POST expense surfaces as 400 even though 'conflict' (409) is more REST-ish; not a bug, matches existing style across the file.
seed_data_creation: test_security_fixes.py seeds in Mongo: users user_sec_test_1 (sec1@quota.local) + user_sec_test_2 (sec2@quota.local), their sessions (sec_token_user_1/2), and configs (parent2_email=delivered@resend.dev) idempotently (xdist-safe upsert with DuplicateKeyError swallow). Blocks created ad-hoc per test class via _create_block helper (blk_sec_<uid>_<month>_<year>). Teardown (_cleanup_db) wipes users/sessions/configs/blocks/email_rate_log for both test users. An additional one-shot post-run cleanup also removed 10 stray email_rate_log entries from the other 2 test modules (user_test + user_close_email_test). Final DB state verified clean: email_rate_log count=0, seed users count=0.
context_for_next_testing_agent: BASE_URL from frontend/.env EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL. pytest.ini mandates -n 2 --dist loadscope; serial run (-n 0) is sanctioned and recommended for this suite because setup_module seeds shared users across workers (upsert handles the race but a serial run is cleaner). Rate-limit tests clear email_rate_log before/after. 3 MB oversize test uses 4.2M-char 'A' base64 payload (~3.15 MB decoded). The close rate limit test resets block.status='open' between calls because _check_rate_limit runs BEFORE the 'already closed' 400 guard - this is intentional per the spec ('contatore e insert' happen first). All future testing agents: do NOT modify pytest.ini addopts, run with -n 0 for determinism on this file.
rca_of_issue: N/A - no bug. All 3 fixes verified: (SEC-002 MIME) text/plain, application/x-sh, application/zip -> 400 'Tipo di allegato non supportato'; image/jpeg, image/png, application/pdf -> 200. Same validation applied on both POST and PUT. (SEC-002 size) base64 payload decoding to > 3*1024*1024 bytes -> 413 'Allegato troppo grande'; <3MB -> 200. Verified on POST and PUT. (SEC-001 close) 11th POST /api/blocks/{id}/close in same hour per user -> 429 'Troppi invii. Riprova piu tardi (massimo 10 ogni 60 minuti).'; first 10 return 200. (SEC-001 resend) 6th POST /api/blocks/{id}/resend-email -> 429; first 5 pass (200 or 502 on email err, both acceptable). (SEC-001 export) 6th POST /api/export/year/{year}/email in 24h -> 429; first 5 -> 200. (SEC-001 isolation) user1 exhausts export quota -> 429 for user1 but user2 same action -> 200 (filter by user_id confirmed per-user).
